findings.comment: `purchaseIDs` filters on `purchaserID` unconditionally, but `purchaserID` was added nullable and is only populated by a separate backfill. While the switch `PURCHASER_READ_SWAP` is off, the purchased feed resolves purchases through `userID`, so a legacy row is listed but the delete lookup cannot find it and returns 400.

finding_contract.current_impact: A user whose purchase row has a null purchaserID (pre-backfill) still sees the set in the purchased feed but gets a 400 on delete and no removal is written.
finding_contract.falsifiable_condition: Run the request with a legacy row.
finding_contract.headline: Delete filters on un-backfilled purchaserID
